standard_prerequisites.name: The statement that a connected component of a space is closed and that a continuous image of a connected space is connected
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 950-954)
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies taking preimages of components and comparing connected subsets.

standard_prerequisites.name: The hypothesis that preimages of points under the map are connected
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof (source lines 955-958)
standard_prerequisites.use: Splits the preimage of a component along the fibres.

core_obligations: Reduce to connectedness of the preimage of a component: every connected subset of the source maps into a component of the target, so it suffices to show that the preimage of a component is connected (proof lines 949-954)
Assume a splitting of that preimage into two closed parts; restricting to a fibre, which is connected, places each fibre in one of the parts (proof lines 955-959)

Descend the splitting: the two parts are preimages of subsets of the component which are closed by the second hypothesis, so the connectedness of the component forces one of them to be empty (proof lines 960-962)
proof_roadmap: 取 Y 的连通分支 T（闭）；只需证 f^{-1}(T) 连通（因 X 的连通子集的像落在某个分支里）。
设 f^{-1}(T) = Z_1 ∐ Z_2（Z_i 闭）；对每个 t ∈ T，由 (1) 知 f^{-1}({t}) 连通 ⇒ 整条纤维落在某个 Z_i 中。
于是 T = T_1 ∐ T_2 且 f^{-1}(T_i) = Z_i；由 (2) 各 T_i 闭；由 T 连通得其一为空。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that a continuous map with connected fibres induces a bijection between the connected components of its source and those of its target (author lemma at source lines 937-947, label lemma-connected-fibres-quotient-topology-connected-components). The proof (source lines 949-963) reduces to connectedness of the preimage of a component, splits a hypothetical separation along the connected fibres and descends the splitting to the component, where connectedness forces one part to be empty (proof lines 949-962). The splitting and descent are the substance. H3.
